description: Bit-width sweep on Llama-3.1-8B and Qwen2.5-14B. Gemma 4 31B attempted but excluded (eval protocol incompatible with instruction-tuned multimodal models on raw WikiText).
hypothesis_confirmed: Two empirically separable failure modes under naive INT quantization. Mode 1 shows INT4 valley of death (ratio >= 100x). Mode 2 is monotonic (ratio 3-10x).

llama_3_1_8b_instruct.note: Meta's cleanest-in-sample recipe. Even naive INT4 is near-perfect (+0.05). 8.9x ratio is ratio-of-small-numbers artifact, not a valley; INT4 is local MIN not local MAX.

qwen2_5_14b.note: Alibaba post-revision recipe. Baseline 1.96 (very low, strong model). Reproduces Phase 6 main-paper naive4 +0.55 approximately (different tokenization/windowing). Same vendor as Qwen2-7B (Mode 1, INT4 +1382), demonstrating a Mode 1 -> Mode 2 transition via recipe revision in 4 months.

gemma_4_31b_it.reason: Baseline PPL 1789 on raw WikiText indicates broken eval protocol for instruction-tuned multimodal models. Model is Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration (multimodal wrapper) and expects chat-formatted input. Raw-text PPL produces near-random predictions with negative ΔPPL artifacts from quantization noise accidentally improving nonsensical baselines. This is not a quantization finding; it's a known evaluation protocol limitation (previously encountered in the norm-separated-quantization V5 Gemma 4 experiments). Would require chat-formatted PPL to evaluate properly.

four_model_dichotomy.separation_factor: Mode 1 ratio (294.7x) is >33x larger than the maximum Mode 2 ratio (8.9x, Llama). This is empirical binary separation.

alibaba_vendor_before_after.implication: The same vendor's recipe revision over 4 months moved the model from Mode 1 catastrophic to Mode 2 monotonic. Training-recipe changes can remove the Layer-0 K outlier pathology entirely.

int3_nsep_pchan_universal.interpretation: INT3 nsep+pchan achieves 5.33x compression with usable quality across all four models. Worst case (Pythia base model) is 22% PPL increase; others are under 15%. This is a candidate practical default for sub-INT4 KV cache deployment.
